tagline.text: A sugarcane town at Cebu's northern tip and the Kawit port for Bantayan

location.label: Location
location.text: Medellin, northern tip of Cebu Island (about 119 km north of Cebu City)

budget.label: Budget
budget.text: About ₱1,500–3,500 (per person, one night, lodging and transport included)

children.text: Medellin is a first-class municipality near the northern end of Cebu Island, a place of sugarcane fields and quiet fishing-village beaches. Ferries to Bantayan Island leave from its Kawit port, so it also serves as a gateway for northern Cebu travel.
Medellin lies about
119 km

north of Cebu City, bordered by Daanbantayan to the north, San Remigio to the southwest and Bogo City to the southeast. With the Tañon Strait to the west and the Camotes Sea to the east, it is a long coastal strip that touches both seas. It covers about 73 km² and has 19 barangays and roughly 62,000 residents (2024 census). The most populous barangays are Kawit, Poblacion and Antipolo.

The town is named after Medellín in Spain and became a municipality in 1881 (September 9) by royal decree of Queen Isabella II, separating from Daanbantayan. It began with three villages—Kawit, Buenavista and Tindog—and, because of pirate threats and shallow waters, the seat of government moved from Kawit to Buenavista and then to Tawagan, which became today's town proper. That history explains why the port and the town center are in different places.

Medellin is often called the "Sugar Bowl of Cebu." Sugarcane is widely grown, and the BOMEDCO sugar mill, founded in 1928, produces raw sugar in Barangay Luy-a. Most residents live by farming and fishing, and tourism is still a promising future rather than a big industry. As a result it is far less crowded than Malapascua or Bantayan, and you can see everyday provincial life up close.

For travelers, Medellin has two faces. One is the Kawit port, the crossing point to Bantayan Island; the other is the white-sand beaches around Kawit, where you can rest quietly. If you are planning a northern Cebu loop or a Bantayan trip, it is a good place to stay a night on the way. During the dry season, which is also the cane-harvest period, trucks on the road can slow your travel.

blocks.title: Kawit port and the Bantayan ferry

children.text: RoRo ferries run from Kawit port to Santa Fe on Bantayan Island. The crossing takes about
55 minutes
, with several departures a day. Since the port opened, Medellin has become known as a new gateway to Bantayan.
Around Kawit there are white-sand beaches and small beach resorts. The white beach near Seahorse Beach Resort is the best known, and on clear days the sea opens up toward Bantayan.

In the dry season, sugarcane fields stretch endlessly along both sides of the road. In harvest season you can see trucks loaded with cane heading to the mill. It is an impressive scene for photography or a scenic drive.

The BOMEDCO mill, opened in 1928 in Luy-a, is the municipality's landmark industrial site. It is not confirmed whether tours are always available, so ask the mill or the municipal office in advance if you want to visit.

The municipal offices and the market are clustered around Poblacion, so you can explore on foot. At the market you can buy fresh seafood and local snacks fairly cheaply, which gives a good look at daily life in a provincial town.

blocks.title: Sunsets and sunrises over two seas

children.text: On the western coast you can watch the sun set over the Tañon Strait, and on the eastern coast see it rise over the Camotes Sea. Having both seas in one municipality is the advantage of its long, narrow shape.

blocks.title: Fishing villages and local fish landings

children.text: In coastal barangays, small bangka boats go out fishing every morning. If you visit a landing early, you can see freshly caught fish and squid being traded, and your host may be able to find fresh seafood for you.

blocks.title: Northern Cebu drive toward Daanbantayan and Bogo

children.text: Heading north from Medellin toward Daanbantayan, the road leads on toward Malapascua, while Bogo City to the south offers a bigger market and more restaurants. It is a convenient midpoint on a northern Cebu loop.
Take a bus bound for Kawit or Medellin from the North Bus Terminal in Cebu City. Depending on traffic it takes about
3–4 hours
, so leave early.
Get off in Medellin town, look around the market and grab a light bite. Take a tricycle to the beaches toward Kawit.
Have lunch at a restaurant near Kawit beach, with grilled fish or shrimp. Check prices before you order.
Rest and swim on the sand. Waves and currents change from day to day, so choose a spot where locals swim.
Check the last bus time and head back. Allow plenty of time for the return trip to Cebu City.
A day trip leaves little time at the beach because of the long travel. If possible, stay one night.

children.text: Leave Cebu City and arrive in Kawit in the early afternoon.
Drop your bags at your lodging and stroll the beach and the port area.
Watch the sunset on the western coast and have dinner at a seafood restaurant.
Get up early to see the fishing village in the morning and the fish landing.

items.title: Flight from Manila, then by road

children.text: From Manila (NAIA) to Mactan-Cebu International Airport (CEB), the direct flight takes about
1 hour 30 minutes
. Airlines operate several flights a day.
From the airport to Medellin you travel north through Cebu City for about
120 km
. A rental car or hired van is easiest; public transport requires transfers.
Flight schedules and fares change often. Check the airline's announcements before booking.

For beaches and boats, the dry season from December to May is best. You can travel in the rainy season too, but boats to Bantayan may be canceled when the sea is rough, so leave some slack in your schedule.

Lodging centers on beach resorts and small guesthouses around Kawit. In high season it fills up with travelers heading to Bantayan, so book ahead. Facilities are modest, so it is safest to confirm air-conditioning, hot water and Wi-Fi before booking.

Grilled fish, shrimp and squid at seaside restaurants are the staples. At the town market you can buy snacks such as puto and bibingka and fresh fruit cheaply. Being sugar country, some places also sell sugarcane juice or brown-sugar sweets. There are not many big restaurants, so it is best to eat dinner before dark.

The Medellin area is a quiet province with almost no big malls or nightlife. It suits people who want to rest, read, or walk on the beach. If you need a convenience store, pharmacy or bank, take care of it in town or in nearby Bogo City beforehand. Buy drinking water and snacks before you head to your lodging.
When going to Bantayan, compare Kawit port with Hagnaya port in San Remigio and choose the one whose timetable suits you.
The last buses tend to stop early, so check your return time first.
Bring plenty of cash. Outside the town ATMs are rare and many places do not take cards.
At the beach, choose a spot where locals swim, and leave valuables at your lodging.
Bring sunscreen, a hat and water. Midday in the dry season has little shade.
Check ferry fares and timetables against the operator's notices and the port counter.
For safety, outsiders may not be allowed into the sugar mill, so get permission before visiting.
In the rainy and typhoon seasons, ferries can suddenly stop because of sea conditions, so leave slack in your Bantayan schedule.
With little public transport, arriving late at night can make it hard to reach your lodging.
Many beaches have no lifeguards, so be extra careful with children.
The September 30, 2025 Cebu earthquake damaged parts of northern Cebu. Check road and facility conditions before you visit.
Fares and timetables change often with fuel surcharges and operator circumstances. Check the latest announcements.
